providers.title: Solvability and coefficient injectivity
providers.scope: An equation w(t)=1 over A is solvable in an overgroup exactly when the coefficient map A -> (A*<t>)/<<w>> is injective. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Coefficient injectivity for unimodular words (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For every group A and every w in A*<t> with exponent sum +-1 the coefficient map is injective; proved in the last lesson from the named statements of the course.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Kervaire conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If A is nontrivial, then (A*<t>)/<<w>> is nontrivial for every w. Uses Theorem 2.1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The regular trace
providers.scope: tau(T) = <T delta_1, delta_1> is tracial, positive and faithful on the commutant of the right translations of any group. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Matrices over the commutant
providers.scope: The trace tau_b on b x b matrices over the commutant is tracial, bounded, positive and faithful. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Functional calculus in the commutant
providers.scope: Bounded Borel functions of a unitary in M_b(M) lie in M_b(M), their traces converge under bounded pointwise convergence, and they transform correctly under unitary conjugation, adjoints and exponentials. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spectral phase
providers.scope: l(U) = tau_b(h(U)) lies in [0,b], vanishes only at the identity, is invariant under conjugation and is the sum of the eigenvalue phases for scalar matrices. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Subadditivity of spectral phase (OpenAI)
providers.scope: l(UV) <= l(U) + l(V) for all unitaries U, V in M_b(M), for every group. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Unitary groups
providers.scope: U(m) is a compact connected smooth manifold of dimension m^2, with exponential charts. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graph charts
providers.scope: k-planes near E_0 are graphs of linear maps, and e^(K_Z) E_0 is the graph of Z tan(sqrt(Z*Z))/sqrt(Z*Z). Uses the inverse function theorem.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The incidence manifold
providers.scope: Pairs (W, E) of a unitary and a k-plane that it fixes form a compact smooth manifold of dimension m^2 - k^2. Uses the inverse function theorem.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The unique preimage
providers.scope: The model map G_(F_0) has exactly one preimage of the identity, at which its derivative is an isomorphism. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A unitary with a large fixed space (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For signs with sum +-1 and every unitary P of size nk, some X in U(k) makes diag(X^(s_1), ..., X^(s_n)) P fix a subspace of dimension k. Uses degree modulo two from the programme.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The planar boundary theorem (OpenAI)
providers.scope: On a connected disk-and-band surface in a sphere for a unimodular word, if all boundary words but one are trivial, so is the last one; proved in the next lesson. Uses (SURF).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Boundary circles
providers.scope: The boundary circles are the cycles of sigma theta, and the boundary words are products of corner labels. Uses (SURF).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Counting boundary circles
providers.scope: A connected surface has k positive and k negative disks, nk bands and nk - 2k + 2 boundary circles. Uses (SURF).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Regions of a connected surface
providers.scope: Each complementary region of a connected disk-and-band surface in a sphere is a disk with one boundary circle. Uses (SURF).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Flows with prescribed circulation
providers.scope: Real phases on the boundary circles with sum zero are realized by antisymmetric numbers on the slots. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The mixing involution
providers.scope: JSJ = S^-1, so SJ is a self-adjoint unitary of trace zero and l(SJ) = nk/2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The upper bound
providers.scope: For a suitable X, J Theta fixes 2k directions and l(S Theta) <= 3nk/2 - k. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Phase of a cycle
providers.scope: l(T_z) = (|z| - 1)/2 + tau(h(e^(2 pi i eta_z) L(r_z^-1))). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spaces for A and A*<t>
providers.scope: A presentation complex Y of A has fundamental group A, and its wedge with a circle has fundamental group A*<t>. Uses (PI1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A piecewise affine circle coordinate
providers.scope: The circle coordinate of a map of a punctured disk can be approximated within 1/12 by a map affine in lifted angles on a triangulation, with the same boundary behaviour. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Level arcs
providers.scope: A generic level of the approximation consists of circles and arcs that pair the occurrences of t with opposite exponents, in a region where the coefficient coordinate is constant. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
